"Christ in Me"

By: Graham Coetzer | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A church that dictates your finances, what meds your children take and who you should marry... Former Christ in Me followers say the church is nothing more than a cult.

Unique Selling Point:
Christ in Me is a church based in Pretoria, with branches in places like Polokwane and Heidelberg as well. They preach a peculiar form of Christianity. They do not believe in the Trinity of God, and they believe that their leader Xandre Strydom is the reincarnation of King David and the new Christ on earth. But former members of the church say they are a cult, responsible for breaking up families and isolating their members from society for the church's own financial gain.

Summary:
The church uses indoctrination and some very questionable teachings to convince members to basically leave every decision they make in life in the hands of the church elders. This has led to families breaking up, divorces and people handing over their life savings and properties to the church.

Further information:
We have confirmed interviews with the following case studies:

Dawie Spies: The uncle of rugby player Pierre Spies, Dawie is a well known christian who is a regular speaker conferences such as Angus Buchan's Mighty Men. Dawie was Xandre' Strydom's mentor and spiritual leader. As Xandre' became a young leader in Dawie's christian outreach program Time Out Ministries, Dawie eventually handed over the whole ministry, with it's bank accounts, equipment and assets to Xandre' with the belief that he would continue the good work. But the very next day Xandre' changed the name and bank accounts to Christ in Me, cut off any contact with Dawie and started his own church. Dawie says it was a complete betrayal. Dawie's good friend Dirk de Bruin might do an interview. Dirk had a daughter who was undergoing Chemo-therapy for cancer. According to Dirk, Xandre' told his daughter to stop the treatment and that God would save her. She did stop chemo, and passed away shortly after.

Cathy: A mother of three who says her whole family was involved with the church. But because of manipulation, such as having to ask the church permission to go on holiday, she left. This has resulted in her divorce from her husband of 35 years and separation from her daughters who are still in the church. She has lost everything.

Drienie: Cathy's daughter who was until two months ago still in the church. Left because of manipulation ie: the church telling her what medicines her young children were allowed to take etc. When she started questioning the church one of the elders publicly humiliated her by "driving out demons" from her in front of the whole congregation. Has lost contact with her father and other siblings who are still in the church.

Hesmarie: Was never in the church but her parents and three siblings all are. The church commanded her family to break contact with her because she was not part of them, which they did. On whatsapp.

Bennie: His wife got involved with the church, and pressured Bennie to also become involved. He attended some of their meetings but was not impressed with the amount of control the church was influencing on his wife. She had to for instance take part in a 50 day event where members had to attend church for 50 days in a row. She also had to attend budget meetings, where she had to disclose all her financial information to the church. She had to ask the church what to do with her R150 000 bonus for example. When Bennie left the church they told his wife she could not stay married to a man who did not share her passion for Christ. Bennie is currently going through a messy divorce because of the church. He is also concerned about the control the church has over his twin daughters lives. He has recently found out that all church members have to have their children evaluated by the church.

Fritz: Was a member since the churches founding in 2010. But soon fell out with them because of the manipulation and control, having to ask permission to buy a car for example. Once he left the church, he says his wife was also manipulated into divorcing him. Is also concerned about the control the church has over his wife and his children.

Wesley: Left the church because of their religious beliefs, the fact that Xandre' sees himself as a new king on earth, and feels they do damge to the community instead of building it up.

We have an email dated 2013, where one of the directors of Christ in Me questions investments the church is making with their congregations funds. He also questions why Xandre' was allowed to lend his father R140 000 of the church's money and distances himself from a R600 000 investment the church is taking from a member, saying the church is misusing funds.

We have a voice recording of Xandre' verbally attacking Cathy for questioning him and the church, taken three days after Cathy had a severe stroke.

We have whatsapp messages from Xandre' to Drienie where Xandre' threatens to make private recordings of Drienie's personal life, which she shared with church elders and were recorded by the church, public on social media.

We have whatsapp voice notes from church elders to Bennie's wife, where she is told to make a choice between Bennie and the church. She is told she is not allowed to attend Bennie's birthday. She is told to setup her "Budget" meeting to discuss the R150 000 bonus.

And we have a voice note to Bennie, where an elder tells him that he has obviously been speaking to other churches about Christ in Me, and that they are misleading him. And that if he does not want to become part of the Christ in Me "family", he will lose his marriage to his wife.

We have still images of a slideshow shown in the church where Xandre' replaces his name, as Xandre' Christ, into biblical versus where the name Jesus Christ appears

We have a copy of the Christ in Me "Marriage Covenant", where the church explains that there are two kinds of people. a 13 person and a 14 person. A thirteen is a "locust", or negative person who has not truly given himself to Christ. A 14 person is a person who is obedient to the Lord and Xandre's version of the kingdom of Christ. The covenant says if a 13 person and a 14 person are married, the marriage will not last and that the church needs to help couples both become 14 people or divorce will be inevitable.

We have copies of Facebook posts where a father takes on the church because he was not allowed to walk his daughter, who is in the church, down the aisle because Xandre will do so and lift the veil from her face in during the ceremony.

We have copies of the Budget documents members are required to fill in, a detailed three pages covering everything from income and expenses to amounts of credit cards, loans etc.

We have copies of a slideshow given in church where Xandre' explains how is the new King David on earth, and how he received supernatural word from God that this is so.

We have hidden camera footage of the "glass cubicles" members are taken into to receive counselling from elders.

JHB & PTA

Press Release:


Church or Cult?
As one member after another leaves a Pretoria-based church group, questions emerge about their brand of Christianity that dismisses the Holy Trinity and allegedly subjects adherents to indoctrination and coercion. Fashioned around the personality of their leader, a self-proclaimed reincarnation of King David and the new Christ on earth, former members say this is a cult that has split apart families and isolated their members from society for the church's financial gain.


Script:


“Christ In Me”

Sound Up Xandre’ Strydom
But isn’t this playing off exactly right now. The second coming of Christ is here.The sign of Jonah is here.

Voice
This is Xandre’ Strydom. He is the vision leader of Christ in Me International, a Pretoria based church with hundreds of followers. They believe they’re ushering in the 2nd coming of Christ. But Strydom has come under fire on social media from many mainstream christians because of his teachings. These include referring to himself as Xandre’ Christ, claiming there is no holy trinity of God, the Son and the Holy Spirit and that he was divinely chosen as king David.

Sound Up Xandre’
People get angry and they say: Who do you think you are, you want to be a king over the people? No no no sir thats your desire hidden in your heart that’s why God didn’t choose you.

Link Devi
Xandre’ believes that he’s preaching a new kind of gospel, but former members of the church say that he’s taking the congregation for a ride.

Voice
Drienie de Beer left Christ in Me earlier this year and says the organisation operates more like a cult than a church.

Sound Up Drienie de Beer
Devi: You’ve called them a cult, do you believe that’s what they are?

Drienie: Yes. Absolutely. And they are very destructive. You go for these sessions with some members of the order, and we call it “inspraak”.

Voice
Inspraak, which can be loosely translated as counsel, takes place inside the church’s headquarters in Pretoria East near the upmarket suburb of Silve Lakes, in these glass cubicles, where the congregation receive counsel from senior Christ in Me members called “Leermeesters” or tutors.

Sound Up Fritz
If you want to buy a house for instance, or you want to buy a car, or if you want to date someone. If they say yes it’s yes, if they say no it’s nohting thorugh them. you have to do every.

Voice
Fritz Broodryk is also a former Christ in Me member who says Strydom and his leermeesters use “Inspraak” to gain complete control over their congregation.

Sound Up Fritz
If they say yes then it’s a yes. Then you can buy a house or start a business. You have to do everyhting through them. If they say yes it’s a yes, if it’s no its no.

Voice
Strydom agreed to an interview with us under the proviso that he be allowed to make his own recording of the conversation. On arrival we were told that Christ in Me’s PR/Legal representative Jaco Elloff would also be sitting in. Strydom is adamant that they are not a cult.

Sound Up Xandre / Jaco
Devi: Now this is not something new, you’ve heard this allegation before?

Xandre’: Yes we have. Unfortunately, but yes we have.

Devi: What’s your response?

Xandre’: No. When we describe and define ourselves, not at all do we believe that we’re a cult. We don’t even believe that we’re a movement, a new movement. Devi with all my heart I do believe that we are the progressive word of God. And I believe that God was going to bring the covenant that he made with Jesus Christ 2000 years ago. All the prophecies said that out of Africa and out of the tip of South Africa will come the last day gospel. And I really believe that this is part of that.

Voice
de Beer says members are expected to share their most intimate personal, marital and financial affairs with the Leermeesters.

Sound Up Drienie
Devi: What did they expect you to say?

Drienie: Everything.Everything that went on in your life, your thoughts. What food to give your children. How to manage your children. How to manage your marriage. Like everything.

Voice
This former congregant, who we’ll call “Timothy”, says the church wants access to all your financial information.

Sound Up “Timothy”
They want to tell you where to do what with what finances, how much money you must give them a month. Where can you invest, how much do you owe on your house. How much is outstanding on your vehicles. Who is your brokers. Life insurance. Short term. All aspects they want.

Voice
Timothy showed us the budget template he says the church wanted him to complete. And it is comprehensive. It lists everything from toiletries to credit cards and policies. Interestingly, the first two entries under expenses are listed as CIM Debit Order 1 and CIM debit order 2.

Sound Up Timothy
There’s definitely something very wrong here.

Voice
de Beer says the she’s been publicly humiliated during Inspraak, when an altercation with a Leermeester led to an embarrassing scene.

Sound Up Drienie
He started driving out devils out of me, and then after that, ja I promise you, but in top voice. And it’s in those glass, those glass cubicles that they have, so everyone can hear and see you. And it was after sunday, so that place was full. So it was very embarrassing.

Voice
Professor Maria Frahm-Arp from the University of Johannesburg’s Department of Religion Studies has spent two decades studying Cults, Pentecostal and Charismatic churches. We didn’t ask her to comment on Christ in Me, only on cults in general to see if the characteristics were similar.

Sound Up Maria
So something isn’t a cult just because it’s new. It’s a cult because it has certain characteristics. These characteristics are generally: cults and their leaders have access to information that you can’t get from anyone else. And only when you join do you begin to get access to this information.

Voice
According to Strydom’s own gospel, his information can help lift the veil from non Christ in Me christian’s eyes.

Sound Up Xandre’
We see things differently then what they see. They look, they can’t see past the flesh of Xandre’ or Neels or Christopher. They cannot see what God is doing. Because they are veil minded. Yes? Yes?

Sound Up Maria
Cults tend to be very hierarchical, everything is focussed on the leader. And so often in academic literature we’ll talk about cult movements as being around the cult of a leader.

Voice
Strydom has admitted publicly that his followers have bowed down to him and called him king, but says he does not ask them to do so. He has also been known to refer to himself as Xandre’ Christ in his presentations to his followers.

Sound Up Xandre/Jaco
Devi: This slide here, Psalm 23 CIM translation, will you just have a look at that for me?

Xandre’: Yes

Devi: Can you read the first line for me please?

Xandre’: The Lord appointed his day 7 lord Xandre’ Christ as our shepherd, therefore we shall not want. Do you want me to go on?

Devi: No just that line.

Xandre’: Ok

Voice
Most Christians would see this kind of statement as the height of blasphemy, but Strydom says it only refers to the original Greek, meaning anointed.

Sound Up Xandre’
The word Christ is defined as anointed. We only took Christ and put it next to Jesus. But Christ is an adjective that is put next to every person that is born again. Jesus was the first Christ.

Voice
After the interview, the church felt they had been unprepared for our questions, and sent an email asking us to add this to Strydom’s answer: Xandre’ believes he is Christ(Anointed) and not Jesus Christ. He refers in sermons to this to teach people who they are as Christ, a born again species.

Sound Up Maria
Very often they’ll ask you to give up connections with your family, give up connections with your friends.








Voice
Hesmarie Louw, who spoke to us from Cape Town via Skype, says her mother and three siblings are all members of Christ in Me. She says when she raised her concerns about the church,her family was instructed to break contact with her.

Sound Up Hesmarie
On the family whatsapp group I just got these messages from them. And they all just copy and pasted the same message, and they all just said listen we understand that you believe differently from us, and we respect that and we want you to also respect us, but we can’t go on like this and we have to go our separate ways.

Voice
Louw says After 6 months of no contact whatsoever,the church sent a Leermeester to see her.

Sound Up Hesmarie
and he did tell me that it was an instruction from them to protect us, that was their words, to protect us from fighting too much.

Voice
She says after the meeting she was allowed to speak to her family again, but that the relationship is still strained.

Sound Up Hesmarie
I miss them. I my family so much. I miss each and every one of them. I miss my brother, I miss my two sisters and I miss my mom most of all. Because I don’t have a relationship with them anymore. They don’t know what’s going on in my life, and I don’t know what’s going on in theirs.

Sound Up Xandre’
Devi: One of the allegations is that Christ in Me breaks up families. So if people don’t want to belong to Christ in Me and they don’t want to come here, people are encouraged to then divorce each other, not speak to children. Your response on that allegation?

Xandre’: That’s not at all true. So we are not the ones persecuting the world, we are a new progressive word from God that is being persecuted. When people can’t adopt to this faith, they start and point finger and say you do this and you do that, and you do this and you do that.

Voice
they also deny forcing people into any financial, parenting or lifestyle decisions.

Sound Up Xandre’
We can’t make people’s decisions for them. We council them on what we would do. But we don’t make people’s decisions for them. People are free to make their own decisions.

Voice
The church says there is nothing unusual about their budget templates, they are simply a mechanism to help people take stock of their finances. But we had another financial question for them.

Sound Up Xandre’
Devi: I’ve got an email here that goes back to 2013 and it’s an email that was written by you Jaco, just explain this to me. I’m going to show you the email but basically what happens it talks about R120 000 worth of vision money that was invested in Xandre’s father’s business. You said that you were very concerned that there were no controls, that it’s unregulated, what happened there?

Jaco Eloff: Well at that moment I was not very much involved with the management, and I saw the figures, and I questioned the board on the figures.

Devi: Did Xandre’ give church money to his father to run a business?

Jaco: Well I cannot elaborate on all that information.

Devi: Why not?

Jaco: Because that was sorted out.

Devi: It doesn’t matter that it was sorted out, did that or did that not happen?

Jaco: From my understanding it did not happen.

Devi: Xandre’?

Xandre’: Ja well…

Devi: Did that happen? Did you give money, church money, to your dad?

Xandre’: We invest our money.

Devi: So the answer is yes?

Xandre’: Yes it’s true.

Voice
In their post interview email they had this to say: Xandre’, on behalf of the NPC, made a loan towards his father’s company. The loan was repaid in full. Since then the organisation has implemented policies and procedures to prevent the mistakes made by us in 2013. Meanwhile, Strydom believes he has been divinely chosen to interpret the word of God, and bring it to the world.

Sound Up Xandre’
But for many years, the gospel was like a fairy tale. It was a big narrative story about a person who died for many people so that they can have eternal life. Our definition according to eternal life wasnt right I believe. And now that story, the bible, is an instruction manual to lead people to lead the same life that Jesus Christ lived.

Voice
Cult or church? We’ll leave it to you to decide.

Release: Church or Cult? As one member after another leaves a Pretoria-based church group, questions emerge about their brand of Christianity that dismisses the Holy Trinity and allegedly subjects adherents to indoctrination and coercion. Fashioned around the personality of their leader, a self-proclaimed reincarnation of King David and the new Christ on earth, former members say this is a cult that has split apart families and isolated their members from society for the church's financial gain. Script: “Christ In Me” Sound Up Xandre’ Strydom But isn’t this playing off exactly right now. The second coming of Christ is here.The sign of Jonah is here. Voice This is Xandre’ Strydom. He is the vision leader of Christ in Me International, a Pretoria based church with hundreds of followers. They believe they’re ushering in the 2nd coming of Christ. But Strydom has come under fire on social media from many mainstream christians because of his teachings. These include referring to himself as Xandre’ Christ, claiming there is no holy trinity of God, the Son and the Holy Spirit and that he was divinely chosen as king David. Sound Up Xandre’ People get angry and they say: Who do you think you are, you want to be a king over the people? No no no sir thats your desire hidden in your heart that’s why God didn’t choose you. Link Devi Xandre’ believes that he’s preaching a new kind of gospel, but former members of the church say that he’s taking the congregation for a ride. Voice Drienie de Beer left Christ in Me earlier this year and says the organisation operates more like a cult than a church. Sound Up Drienie de Beer Devi: You’ve called them a cult, do you believe that’s what they are? Drienie: Yes. Absolutely. And they are very destructive. You go for these sessions with some members of the order, and we call it “inspraak”. Voice Inspraak, which can be loosely translated as counsel, takes place inside the church’s headquarters in Pretoria East near the upmarket suburb of Silve Lakes, in these glass cubicles, where the congregation receive counsel from senior Christ in Me members called “Leermeesters” or tutors. Sound Up Fritz If you want to buy a house for instance, or you want to buy a car, or if you want to date someone. If they say yes it’s yes, if they say no it’s nohting thorugh them. you have to do every. Voice Fritz Broodryk is also a former Christ in Me member who says Strydom and his leermeesters use “Inspraak” to gain complete control over their congregation. Sound Up Fritz If they say yes then it’s a yes. Then you can buy a house or start a business. You have to do everyhting through them. If they say yes it’s a yes, if it’s no its no. Voice Strydom agreed to an interview with us under the proviso that he be allowed to make his own recording of the conversation. On arrival we were told that Christ in Me’s PR/Legal representative Jaco Elloff would also be sitting in. Strydom is adamant that they are not a cult. Sound Up Xandre / Jaco Devi: Now this is not something new, you’ve heard this allegation before? Xandre’: Yes we have. Unfortunately, but yes we have. Devi: What’s your response? Xandre’: No. When we describe and define ourselves, not at all do we believe that we’re a cult. We don’t even believe that we’re a movement, a new movement. Devi with all my heart I do believe that we are the progressive word of God. And I believe that God was going to bring the covenant that he made with Jesus Christ 2000 years ago. All the prophecies said that out of Africa and out of the tip of South Africa will come the last day gospel. And I really believe that this is part of that. Voice de Beer says members are expected to share their most intimate personal, marital and financial affairs with the Leermeesters. Sound Up Drienie Devi: What did they expect you to say? Drienie: Everything.Everything that went on in your life, your thoughts. What food to give your children. How to manage your children. How to manage your marriage. Like everything. Voice This former congregant, who we’ll call “Timothy”, says the church wants access to all your financial information. Sound Up “Timothy” They want to tell you where to do what with what finances, how much money you must give them a month. Where can you invest, how much do you owe on your house. How much is outstanding on your vehicles. Who is your brokers. Life insurance. Short term. All aspects they want. Voice Timothy showed us the budget template he says the church wanted him to complete. And it is comprehensive. It lists everything from toiletries to credit cards and policies. Interestingly, the first two entries under expenses are listed as CIM Debit Order 1 and CIM debit order 2. Sound Up Timothy There’s definitely something very wrong here. Voice de Beer says the she’s been publicly humiliated during Inspraak, when an altercation with a Leermeester led to an embarrassing scene. Sound Up Drienie He started driving out devils out of me, and then after that, ja I promise you, but in top voice. And it’s in those glass, those glass cubicles that they have, so everyone can hear and see you. And it was after sunday, so that place was full. So it was very embarrassing. Voice Professor Maria Frahm-Arp from the University of Johannesburg’s Department of Religion Studies has spent two decades studying Cults, Pentecostal and Charismatic churches. We didn’t ask her to comment on Christ in Me, only on cults in general to see if the characteristics were similar. Sound Up Maria So something isn’t a cult just because it’s new. It’s a cult because it has certain characteristics. These characteristics are generally: cults and their leaders have access to information that you can’t get from anyone else. And only when you join do you begin to get access to this information. Voice According to Strydom’s own gospel, his information can help lift the veil from non Christ in Me christian’s eyes. Sound Up Xandre’ We see things differently then what they see. They look, they can’t see past the flesh of Xandre’ or Neels or Christopher. They cannot see what God is doing. Because they are veil minded. Yes? Yes? Sound Up Maria Cults tend to be very hierarchical, everything is focussed on the leader. And so often in academic literature we’ll talk about cult movements as being around the cult of a leader. Voice Strydom has admitted publicly that his followers have bowed down to him and called him king, but says he does not ask them to do so. He has also been known to refer to himself as Xandre’ Christ in his presentations to his followers. Sound Up Xandre/Jaco Devi: This slide here, Psalm 23 CIM translation, will you just have a look at that for me? Xandre’: Yes Devi: Can you read the first line for me please? Xandre’: The Lord appointed his day 7 lord Xandre’ Christ as our shepherd, therefore we shall not want. Do you want me to go on? Devi: No just that line. Xandre’: Ok Voice Most Christians would see this kind of statement as the height of blasphemy, but Strydom says it only refers to the original Greek, meaning anointed. Sound Up Xandre’ The word Christ is defined as anointed. We only took Christ and put it next to Jesus. But Christ is an adjective that is put next to every person that is born again. Jesus was the first Christ. Voice After the interview, the church felt they had been unprepared for our questions, and sent an email asking us to add this to Strydom’s answer: Xandre’ believes he is Christ(Anointed) and not Jesus Christ. He refers in sermons to this to teach people who they are as Christ, a born again species. Sound Up Maria Very often they’ll ask you to give up connections with your family, give up connections with your friends. Voice Hesmarie Louw, who spoke to us from Cape Town via Skype, says her mother and three siblings are all members of Christ in Me. She says when she raised her concerns about the church,her family was instructed to break contact with her. Sound Up Hesmarie On the family whatsapp group I just got these messages from them. And they all just copy and pasted the same message, and they all just said listen we understand that you believe differently from us, and we respect that and we want you to also respect us, but we can’t go on like this and we have to go our separate ways. Voice Louw says After 6 months of no contact whatsoever,the church sent a Leermeester to see her. Sound Up Hesmarie and he did tell me that it was an instruction from them to protect us, that was their words, to protect us from fighting too much. Voice She says after the meeting she was allowed to speak to her family again, but that the relationship is still strained. Sound Up Hesmarie I miss them. I my family so much. I miss each and every one of them. I miss my brother, I miss my two sisters and I miss my mom most of all. Because I don’t have a relationship with them anymore. They don’t know what’s going on in my life, and I don’t know what’s going on in theirs. Sound Up Xandre’ Devi: One of the allegations is that Christ in Me breaks up families. So if people don’t want to belong to Christ in Me and they don’t want to come here, people are encouraged to then divorce each other, not speak to children. Your response on that allegation? Xandre’: That’s not at all true. So we are not the ones persecuting the world, we are a new progressive word from God that is being persecuted. When people can’t adopt to this faith, they start and point finger and say you do this and you do that, and you do this and you do that. Voice they also deny forcing people into any financial, parenting or lifestyle decisions. Sound Up Xandre’ We can’t make people’s decisions for them. We council them on what we would do. But we don’t make people’s decisions for them. People are free to make their own decisions. Voice The church says there is nothing unusual about their budget templates, they are simply a mechanism to help people take stock of their finances. But we had another financial question for them. Sound Up Xandre’ Devi: I’ve got an email here that goes back to 2013 and it’s an email that was written by you Jaco, just explain this to me. I’m going to show you the email but basically what happens it talks about R120 000 worth of vision money that was invested in Xandre’s father’s business. You said that you were very concerned that there were no controls, that it’s unregulated, what happened there? Jaco Eloff: Well at that moment I was not very much involved with the management, and I saw the figures, and I questioned the board on the figures. Devi: Did Xandre’ give church money to his father to run a business? Jaco: Well I cannot elaborate on all that information. Devi: Why not? Jaco: Because that was sorted out. Devi: It doesn’t matter that it was sorted out, did that or did that not happen? Jaco: From my understanding it did not happen. Devi: Xandre’? Xandre’: Ja well… Devi: Did that happen? Did you give money, church money, to your dad? Xandre’: We invest our money. Devi: So the answer is yes? Xandre’: Yes it’s true. Voice In their post interview email they had this to say: Xandre’, on behalf of the NPC, made a loan towards his father’s company. The loan was repaid in full. Since then the organisation has implemented policies and procedures to prevent the mistakes made by us in 2013. Meanwhile, Strydom believes he has been divinely chosen to interpret the word of God, and bring it to the world. Sound Up Xandre’ But for many years, the gospel was like a fairy tale. It was a big narrative story about a person who died for many people so that they can have eternal life. Our definition according to eternal life wasnt right I believe. And now that story, the bible, is an instruction manual to lead people to lead the same life that Jesus Christ lived. Voice Cult or church? We’ll leave it to you to decide.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A church that dictates your finances, what meds your children take and who you should marry... Former Christ in Me followers say the church is nothing more than a cult.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Christ in Me is a church based in Pretoria, with branches in places like Polokwane and Heidelberg as well. They preach a peculiar form of Christianity. They do not believe in the Trinity of God, and they believe that their leader Xandre Strydom is the reincarnation of King David and the new Christ on earth. But former members of the church say they are a cult, responsible for breaking up families and isolating their members from society for the church's own financial gain.
metadata.Summary: The church uses indoctrination and some very questionable teachings to convince members to basically leave every decision they make in life in the hands of the church elders. This has led to families breaking up, divorces and people handing over their life savings and properties to the church.
metadata.Further information: We have confirmed interviews with the following case studies: Dawie Spies: The uncle of rugby player Pierre Spies, Dawie is a well known christian who is a regular speaker conferences such as Angus Buchan's Mighty Men. Dawie was Xandre' Strydom's mentor and spiritual leader. As Xandre' became a young leader in Dawie's christian outreach program Time Out Ministries, Dawie eventually handed over the whole ministry, with it's bank accounts, equipment and assets to Xandre' with the belief that he would continue the good work. But the very next day Xandre' changed the name and bank accounts to Christ in Me, cut off any contact with Dawie and started his own church. Dawie says it was a complete betrayal. Dawie's good friend Dirk de Bruin might do an interview. Dirk had a daughter who was undergoing Chemo-therapy for cancer. According to Dirk, Xandre' told his daughter to stop the treatment and that God would save her. She did stop chemo, and passed away shortly after. Cathy: A mother of three who says her whole family was involved with the church. But because of manipulation, such as having to ask the church permission to go on holiday, she left. This has resulted in her divorce from her husband of 35 years and separation from her daughters who are still in the church. She has lost everything. Drienie: Cathy's daughter who was until two months ago still in the church. Left because of manipulation ie: the church telling her what medicines her young children were allowed to take etc. When she started questioning the church one of the elders publicly humiliated her by "driving out demons" from her in front of the whole congregation. Has lost contact with her father and other siblings who are still in the church. Hesmarie: Was never in the church but her parents and three siblings all are. The church commanded her family to break contact with her because she was not part of them, which they did. On whatsapp. Bennie: His wife got involved with the church, and pressured Bennie to also become involved. He attended some of their meetings but was not impressed with the amount of control the church was influencing on his wife. She had to for instance take part in a 50 day event where members had to attend church for 50 days in a row. She also had to attend budget meetings, where she had to disclose all her financial information to the church. She had to ask the church what to do with her R150 000 bonus for example. When Bennie left the church they told his wife she could not stay married to a man who did not share her passion for Christ. Bennie is currently going through a messy divorce because of the church. He is also concerned about the control the church has over his twin daughters lives. He has recently found out that all church members have to have their children evaluated by the church. Fritz: Was a member since the churches founding in 2010. But soon fell out with them because of the manipulation and control, having to ask permission to buy a car for example. Once he left the church, he says his wife was also manipulated into divorcing him. Is also concerned about the control the church has over his wife and his children. Wesley: Left the church because of their religious beliefs, the fact that Xandre' sees himself as a new king on earth, and feels they do damge to the community instead of building it up. We have an email dated 2013, where one of the directors of Christ in Me questions investments the church is making with their congregations funds. He also questions why Xandre' was allowed to lend his father R140 000 of the church's money and distances himself from a R600 000 investment the church is taking from a member, saying the church is misusing funds. We have a voice recording of Xandre' verbally attacking Cathy for questioning him and the church, taken three days after Cathy had a severe stroke. We have whatsapp messages from Xandre' to Drienie where Xandre' threatens to make private recordings of Drienie's personal life, which she shared with church elders and were recorded by the church, public on social media. We have whatsapp voice notes from church elders to Bennie's wife, where she is told to make a choice between Bennie and the church. She is told she is not allowed to attend Bennie's birthday. She is told to setup her "Budget" meeting to discuss the R150 000 bonus. And we have a voice note to Bennie, where an elder tells him that he has obviously been speaking to other churches about Christ in Me, and that they are misleading him. And that if he does not want to become part of the Christ in Me "family", he will lose his marriage to his wife. We have still images of a slideshow shown in the church where Xandre' replaces his name, as Xandre' Christ, into biblical versus where the name Jesus Christ appears We have a copy of the Christ in Me "Marriage Covenant", where the church explains that there are two kinds of people. a 13 person and a 14 person. A thirteen is a "locust", or negative person who has not truly given himself to Christ. A 14 person is a person who is obedient to the Lord and Xandre's version of the kingdom of Christ. The covenant says if a 13 person and a 14 person are married, the marriage will not last and that the church needs to help couples both become 14 people or divorce will be inevitable. We have copies of Facebook posts where a father takes on the church because he was not allowed to walk his daughter, who is in the church, down the aisle because Xandre will do so and lift the veil from her face in during the ceremony. We have copies of the Budget documents members are required to fill in, a detailed three pages covering everything from income and expenses to amounts of credit cards, loans etc. We have copies of a slideshow given in church where Xandre' explains how is the new King David on earth, and how he received supernatural word from God that this is so. We have hidden camera footage of the "glass cubicles" members are taken into to receive counselling from elders.
